evidence.quote: (B) ER visits: TM vs. no TM

limitations: Disposition aggregate_only: the source is a 10-participant feasibility study of iPad telemedicine in spinal cord injury reported only as counts, means, percentages and survey frequencies; no participant has individual identity evidence or an individually described course, so no individual patient records are created and cohort statements are not copied to placeholder patients.
reported_individual_count is 10 (literal, "Ten participants were enrolled") and roster_complete is false because none of the 10 individuals can be enumerated.
Quality-of-life and satisfaction results cover 8 of the 10 participants (two did not complete the 6-month follow-up); these group results are not attributed to individuals.

The abstract reports age as "34.4 (18-54) years" while Table 1 and the results print "34.4 ± 14.4" (mean ± SD); these are different statistics for the same mean, not a conflict, and neither is attributed to an individual.

The text says half of the participants did not use telemedicine in the study and that "five participants did not utilize FaceTime appointments"; it reports 16 physician TM visits in total. These counts are consistent (the visits came from the other participants) and are recorded as printed without attribution to individuals.

Table 2 prints one set of column headers for all rows although several questions (N-R) use different answer categories in separate header rows; the table is aggregate and no cell is attributed to an individual participant.
Anecdotal comments in Table 2 are unattributed participant quotes and are not assigned to any patient.

Results text b00060 and b00106 mention single unnamed participants ("one person felt more comfortable continuing to see a local physician in-person", "another patient was able to coordinate appointment times", "A participant noted"); these carry no identity evidence, demographics or individual clinical course, cannot be linked to any enrolled participant, and are not made into patient records.
Figures 1 and 2 are a process flow diagram and group-level charts; their pixels are described only in visual.json and no patient is assigned.
No supplements are listed by the source.
